observation.visible_scene: A white tabletop. In the blurred background sit two magnetic-ball structures: a plain silver sphere on the left and a sphere with embedded green LED lights on the right. In the foreground, from left to right, are a human fingertip at the edge of frame, a small silver cube magnet, a straight row/strip of small rectangular magnets, and a compact mound of blue granular material at the near end of the magnet strip.
visible_changes: The small silver cube magnet tilts and rotates in place, then translates rightward toward the magnet strip, reaching and overlapping the blue mound by about t=0.4 s (with motion blur).

The blue mound deforms rather than simply moving: it first rises into standing spike/brush tufts around the cube and the near end of the strip (t≈0.5–0.6 s), then spreads outward into a large curved blue fan/brush that lies along the magnet strip (t≈0.7–1.2 s).

The blue fan/brush persists for the remainder of the clip, slowly flattening and spreading a little more while the cube stays embedded at the near end of the strip; the magnet strip itself does not move.
The fingertip at the left edge gradually withdraws toward the bottom-left and is nearly gone by the end.
The green LED pattern on the right background sphere flickers/changes subtly between frames.
outside_clip_unknowns: No hand contact with the cube is clearly visible, so what initiated the cube's rightward motion is not shown.
Whether the blue brush continues to settle, collapses, or holds its shape after t=2.667 s is outside the excerpt.
The state before t=0 (how the blue mound and cube were placed) is not shown.
uncertain_details: Background spheres stay nearly fixed in frame, so the dominant motion is object-based; any camera zoom/shift is slight and uncertain.
The exact instant of cube–strip/blue contact is obscured by motion blur around t=0.4–0.5 s.
The blue material's identity (filings/putty) is inferred from appearance only; not stated as a fact.
